understanding-fractions-skill-01.target: I can name the unit fraction 1/b for one of b equal parts of a whole and tell whether parts are equal.
understanding-fractions-skill-01.ifCorrect: You can do this: can name the unit fraction 1/b for one of b equal parts of a whole and tell whether parts are equal.
understanding-fractions-skill-01.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Naming a fraction for parts that are not equal, or writing the number of shaded parts over unshaded parts. Try this: Ask “Are all the parts the same size?” first; the denominator counts all the equal parts.

understanding-fractions-skill-02.target: I can explain that a/b is a copies of 1/b and name a fraction shown by a model or a story.
understanding-fractions-skill-02.ifCorrect: You can do this: can explain that a/b is a copies of 1/b and name a fraction shown by a model or a story.
understanding-fractions-skill-02.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Thinking a bigger denominator means bigger pieces, or counting unshaded parts as the numerator. Try this: Count unit fractions aloud: one‑fourth, two‑fourths, three‑fourths. The numerator counts how many parts.

understanding-fractions-skill-03.skill: Unit Fractions on a Number Line
understanding-fractions-skill-03.target: I can partition the interval from 0 to 1 into b equal parts and locate 1/b on a number line.
understanding-fractions-skill-03.ifCorrect: You can do this: can partition the interval from 0 to 1 into b equal parts and locate 1/b on a number line.
understanding-fractions-skill-03.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Counting the tick marks instead of the spaces, so thirds become fourths. Try this: Count the jumps (spaces) from 0 to 1, not the marks. Shade the first jump.

understanding-fractions-skill-04.target: I can locate a/b on a number line by marking off a lengths of 1/b from 0, including fractions greater than 1.
understanding-fractions-skill-04.ifCorrect: You can do this: can locate a/b on a number line by marking off a lengths of 1/b from 0, including fractions greater than 1.
understanding-fractions-skill-04.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Starting to count at the first tick mark instead of at 0, or relabeling past 1 as 1/b again. Try this: Make a jump for each unit fraction starting at 0 and count the jumps aloud; keep the same denominator past 1.
